Regulator pages last checked: 27 November 2026.
United Kingdom
The GMC (doctors, OET Medicine) and the NMC (nurses and midwives) accept OET@Home. The GPhC (pharmacists) does not. The HCPC names only OET on Computer and OET on Paper, so OET@Home is not confirmed: treat it as not accepted unless the HCPC tells you otherwise in writing. The GDC page does not name OET at all, so nothing is confirmed for dentists.
Ireland
NMBI (nurses and midwives), the Medical Council (doctors) and the PSI (pharmacists) do not accept it. CORU (health and social care professionals) says online or at-home versions are accepted for OET, although its page does not use the name OET@Home. Because the page never names OET@Home, the table lists CORU as not confirmed: ask CORU in writing before you rely on it.
Australia
Ahpra and the National Boards do not accept OET@Home: they accept OET on paper, or on computer in a testing centre. The Department of Home Affairs does not accept it for visas either.
New Zealand
The Nursing Council of New Zealand does not accept online tests such as OET@Home. For the Medical Council , the Pharmacy Council and the Physiotherapy Board it is not confirmed: their pages say nothing about the delivery mode.
United States
ECFMG (doctors) is conditional: OET@Home only for applicants with no physical test venue in their country. TruMerit , formerly CGFNS (nurses), does not accept at-home versions of English tests. NABP (pharmacists, FPGEC) does not accept home editions of OET or TOEFL iBT; it accepts OET Pharmacy only for tests taken on or after 11 January 2027, at an approved computer-based test centre in the United States, its territories or Canada. See OET for pharmacists in the USA . FCCPT (physical therapists) and the state nursing boards: not confirmed.
Canada
BCCNM (nurses in British Columbia) accepts OET in person only. The national pharmacy policy of NAPRA is conditional: remotely proctored tests can be accepted if they keep the same level of security, each provincial pharmacy regulator decides, and the policy does not name OET@Home. The College of Nurses of Ontario, CPSO, MCC, NNAS and PEBC: not confirmed.
Singapore
Not confirmed. The Singapore Medical Council and the Singapore Pharmacy Council state OET scores but no delivery mode, and we found no Singapore Nursing Board page listing accepted English tests.
Gulf countries
Not confirmed. The Gulf regulators we checked publish no rule on OET@Home. Where an employer asks for OET, ask that employer which mode it accepts. These countries also have OET venues, so OET@Home is normally not bookable there in the first place.
Before you pay Ask your regulator, in writing, whether it accepts OET@Home for your profession and route. OET gives the same instruction in its regulations: check with your recognising organisation that the test mode you have chosen is accepted. Score rules are in OET score requirements , and the rules on combining sittings are in OET clubbing rules .
Question 3: is online Speaking the same as OET@Home?
No. A test is OET@Home only when all four sub-tests are taken at home under remote proctoring. A venue-based test can still include Speaking by video.
OET on Computer at a venue
Listening, Reading and Writing are sat in an approved test centre. Speaking is, in OET's words, &ldquo;conducted at home via a secure platform or for select countries, conducted at venue&rdquo; ( OET on Computer ). OET lists the countries with Speaking at a venue . This is still OET on Computer, not OET@Home.
Regulators treat the two differently
Ahpra does not accept OET@Home, yet it states that the computer test taken in a testing centre, with its one remotely proctored element, is acceptable. The Nursing Council of New Zealand refuses online tests but accepts OET on computer at an approved venue with the Speaking sub-test hosted online.
Paper tests from January 2027
From January 2027 paper candidates (Nursing and Medicine only) still attend a venue for Speaking, and depending on the venue they meet the interlocutor in person or over a live video connection. That is also not OET@Home. Details: the January 2027 paper-test changes .
One regulator to ask
The PSI in Ireland says home-based tests are not accepted and notes that Speaking is delivered at home for OET on Computer candidates, without saying in so many words that this is acceptable. If you are a pharmacist applying to the PSI, confirm with the PSI before you book.
When you book OET on Computer OET's booking page asks you to make sure the Speaking mode you select is accepted by the organisation you are applying to. The two venue formats are compared in OET on computer vs paper .
Equipment, room and ID rules
These are the rules OET states in its Test Regulations (section 6.2) and its OET@Home test day guide of 19 June 2026. Exact system figures are in the OET@Home User Guide, which we have not quoted here.
Equipment
A computer with a video-enabled camera, speakers and a microphone for all sub-tests.
Prometric's ProProctor application for Listening, Reading and Writing, and a secure browser for Speaking.
A wired headset for Listening. Bluetooth headphones are not allowed.
No headphones during the Speaking sub-test.
One screen only: additional monitors are not allowed. VPNs, virtual machines and Bluetooth must be off.
Room
A walled, indoor, well-lit space with no transparent glass walls or partitions.
You must be alone in a quiet room, with no CCTV.
All tests are monitored by video and audio recording.
For Speaking, the interlocutor checks you in and carries out a 360-degree check of the room.
ID
You upload an image of your ID when you book, and you must show the same, original document on test day. Copies are not accepted.
A valid passport, or a valid national ID issued by the government of the country where you sit the test, in English lettering.
A driving licence is not an acceptable ID, with one exception OET states for candidates testing in the United States.
On the day
Log on at least 15 minutes before your scheduled start time.
There is one scheduled 10-minute break, after Reading Part A only.
Speaking is on a different day in the same test administration.
Sources: OET Test Regulations , OET@Home test day guide , test day guide, part 3 (Speaking) , test day information .
When do OET@Home results arrive?
OET says OET@Home results can arrive as early as 48 hours after you have completed all sub-tests. That is the earliest case, not a promise.
Plan with a margin For the computer test at a venue OET adds that 95% of results are released within 6 calendar days. Whether that figure also applies to OET@Home is not confirmed, because the OET@Home page does not state it. ECFMG, for its own applicants, says OET Medicine results typically reach it 10 business days after the test. If you have a registration deadline, count back from the slowest of these.

OET@Home FAQ
What is OET@Home?
OET@Home is the full OET test taken at home on your own computer with remote proctoring. It is one of three delivery modes, next to the OET Test on Paper and the OET Test on Computer at a venue, and it has the same content, timing and marking.
Can I take OET@Home from any country?
No. OET offers OET@Home where taking the test at a venue is not yet available, or as an exception approved case by case. OET publishes no country list, so check the official booking tool for your city. If your country has a test venue, plan to sit at a venue.
Which professions can take OET@Home?
The official sources disagree. OET's own page lists all 12 professions, while the Cambridge English overview lists four: Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and Physiotherapy. Check your profession in the booking tool before you rely on OET@Home.
Which regulators accept OET@Home?
On their own pages, the GMC and the NMC accept it, and ECFMG accepts it only when your country has no physical test venue. CORU says at-home versions are accepted for OET without naming OET@Home, so we list it as not confirmed. The GPhC, NMBI, the Medical Council of Ireland, the PSI, Ahpra, the Australian Department of Home Affairs, the Nursing Council of New Zealand, TruMerit, NABP and BCCNM do not. For many others it is not confirmed, so ask your regulator in writing.
Is online Speaking the same as OET@Home?
No. On the OET Test on Computer you sit Listening, Reading and Writing at a venue, and Speaking may be taken at home or at a venue depending on the country. That is still a venue-based test. OET@Home means all four sub-tests are taken at home.
How much does OET@Home cost?
OET shows a fee of AU$587 for OET@Home, the same as the paper and computer tests. In the United States the fee is US$455. OET does not publish local-currency prices or say whether tax is added.
How fast are OET@Home results?
OET says results can arrive as early as 48 hours after you complete all sub-tests. That is the earliest case, not a guarantee, so leave a margin before any registration deadline.
What equipment do I need for OET@Home?
A computer with a camera, speakers and a microphone, Prometric's ProProctor application, a wired headset for Listening and a single screen. You must be alone in a quiet, walled, well-lit room and show the original ID you used to book.

Paper, computer or OET@Home: what each one means
OET has three test modes. The content, length and marking are the same. Where you sit, who can book and how Speaking runs are different.
OET on Paper OET on Computer (at a venue) OET@Home
Where you sit it At an approved test venue At an approved test venue: Listening, Reading and Writing together On your own computer, with remote proctoring
Professions from January 2027 Nursing and Medicine only All 12 professions, subject to availability OET’s page lists all 12 professions. Cambridge English’s overview lists four: Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and Physiotherapy. Check your profession in the booking tool.
Where it is offered From 2027, in 16 countries according to an OET customer-care email of November 2026. Never guaranteed. In countries with approved computer venues. Not every date or mode is available in every country. OET says it is offered in countries where taking the test at a venue is not yet available. OET publishes no country list.
Speaking At the venue. From January 2027: in person or over a live video connection, depending on the venue. At home on a secure platform or, in select countries, at the venue. On the OET Speaking platform, with a live interlocutor.
Booking closes 24 days before the test date (subject to change) 7 days before the test date 7 days before the test date
OET’s fee AU$587 AU$587 (US$455 in the United States) AU$587 (US$455 in the United States)
What changes in January 2027 OET on Paper continues for Nursing and Medicine only, and paper Speaking may run over a live video connection at the venue. Speaking by video at a venue is not OET@Home: you still attend the venue. See the 16 paper countries and their venues , what OET announced for 2027 , the OET@Home guide and computer vs paper: how to prepare .
If your country has no venue in this directory
This directory covers 26 countries
These are the countries we have checked so far, not OET’s full list. For any other country, search the official finder : it is the only complete source.
If the finder shows no venue either
Two separate questions decide your next step. First, can you book OET@Home from your country and for your profession? That is OET’s rule. Second, will your regulator accept an OET@Home result? That is the regulator’s rule. The OET@Home guide takes both in turn, and OET recognition by country shows who accepts OET for your profession.
How to book an OET test
The official steps, from OET’s booking help article and its Test Regulations .
1. Search the finder
Open oet.com/test/book-a-test , enter your city and country and select Find a test. Filter by test mode or distance, then select Book now on the venue you want.
2. OET on Paper
Register or log in to your myOET account, choose Apply for the test and follow the prompts. Paper candidates upload a photo. Payment must be completed within 15 minutes to secure the booking.
3. OET on Computer and OET@Home
Book through OET’s booking portal from your OET account. You upload an image of your ID, and you have 15 minutes to complete the booking once you select a date.
4. Confirmation
A confirmation email follows, so check your junk folder. OET recommends booking on a desktop or laptop, with a Visa or MasterCard and your ID to hand. You can hold one booking for each test administration, across all modes.
ID on test day
OET publishes one general ID rule, not a country-by-country table ( test day information , ID help article ).
What is accepted
A valid passport.
Or a valid national ID issued by the government of the country where you sit the test, showing your full name, photograph and date of birth on the one document.
For OET on Computer and OET@Home, a national ID must be in English lettering. If it is not, bring a certified translated copy together with the original.
What catches candidates out
The ID you present must be the ID you booked with, and it must be the original document.
A driving licence is not accepted. OET states one exception for candidates testing in the United States, where REAL ID-compliant licences are accepted.
With the wrong ID you may be refused entry, and OET says you may not be entitled to a deferral or refund.
National ID cards OET does not publish a rule for any specific country’s ID card. If you plan to use a national ID instead of a passport, check it against the rule above before you book, and use your passport if you are unsure.
The OET test fee
OET states a test fee of AU$587 for OET on Paper, OET on Computer and OET@Home. In the United States the fee is US$455 for OET on Computer at a venue and for OET@Home ( OET fee help article ).
OET publishes no tax amount and no local-currency price, so we do not state one. Your bank’s exchange rate decides what you pay in your own currency. For the full picture see OET exam fees and OET test dates and fees .
How the Speaking sub-test is delivered
OET on Computer at a venue
You sit Listening, Reading and Writing at the venue. Speaking is taken at home on a secure platform or, in select countries, at the venue ( oet.com ). OET asks you to make sure the Speaking mode you select is accepted by the organisation you are applying to.
Countries with Speaking at a venue
In an oet.com post dated 20 July 2026 , OET listed: Kenya, South Africa, New Zealand, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Australia (Melbourne, Sydney), Nigeria (Lagos), the Philippines, Uganda, Nepal, Ghana (Accra), Bangladesh, India (Mumbai, Gurgaon) and Pakistan (Islamabad, Karachi and Lahore). Egypt, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada, Turkey and Sri Lanka are not on that list. Re-check before booking.
OET on Paper
Speaking is at the venue. Until December 2026 it is face to face. From January 2027 it is in person or over a live video connection, depending on the venue.
OET@Home
Speaking runs on the OET Speaking platform with a live interlocutor.
Speaking may be on a different day For OET on Computer and OET@Home, Speaking can fall on a different day from the other three sub-tests. OET’s own pages give different figures for the gap, so rely on the date and time shown in your booking.
Rescheduling and cancelling, in brief
From section 9 of OET’s Test Regulations , read on 27 November 2026. Fees and deadlines can change, so read the current regulations before you act.
Rescheduling
A full test costs AU$120 to reschedule before the booking closing date and AU$200 after it.
OET on Paper cannot be rescheduled after 11:59pm local time on the day before the test.
OET on Computer: AU$200 applies up to 48 hours before the test and, through customer care, inside the last 48 hours.
You cannot change test mode or profession by rescheduling, or move a computer or OET@Home test to another country. Cancel and rebook instead.
Cancelling
The cancellation fee is AU$120 before the booking closing date and AU$200 after it.
OET on Paper can be cancelled up to one week before the test day.
OET on Computer and OET@Home can be cancelled up to 48 hours before the test start time, and not once a sub-test has been taken.
A no-show without extenuating circumstances gets no refund.
More detail: OET cancellation and refund policy .
Test dates published so far
The paper dates OET has published so far for 2027 are 22, 23, 29 and 30 January, for Nursing and Medicine only. No later paper date was published when we checked on 27 November 2026. OET publishes dates in global tables, not for each venue, so a published date does not mean every venue runs it.
The full tables, with booking windows and results dates, are on OET test dates and fees .

Frequently asked questions
Where can I find OET test centres near me?
Use OET's official venue finder at oet.com/test/book-a-test: enter your city and country and select Find a test. This page lists the venues we read in that finder on 27 November 2026 for 26 countries, grouped by country and city.
Does a venue on this list mean I can book a seat there?
No. A listing shows that the venue is in OET's finder. It does not show that a date or a seat is open. Confirm in the finder before you plan travel.
Are you affiliated with any OET test centre?
No. We are an independent OET coaching service. We are not affiliated with OET or with any test centre, the centres are not our locations and we do not take test bookings.
How much is the OET test fee?
OET states a fee of AU$587 for each test mode. In the United States the fee is US$455 for OET on Computer at a venue and for OET@Home. OET does not publish a tax or local-currency price.
What ID do I need on test day?
A valid passport, or a valid national ID issued by the government of the country where you sit the test, showing your full name, photograph and date of birth. It must be the same original document you used to book.
My country has no OET venue. Can I take OET@Home?
Those are two separate questions. OET decides whether you can book OET@Home from your country and profession, and your regulator decides whether it accepts an OET@Home result. Check both before you book.
Which paper test dates are published for 2027?
When we checked on 27 November 2026, OET had published paper dates on 22, 23, 29 and 30 January 2027, for Nursing and Medicine only. Bookings for OET on Paper close 24 days before the test date.

## OET Paper Test Centres 2027: The 16 Countries | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-paper-test-centres-2027.html

From January 2027 OET on Paper continues for Nursing and Medicine only. See the 16 countries, the paper venues OET lists in each one and the January dates.

Exam Format
OET paper test centres 2027: the 16 countries and their venues
From January 2027, OET on Paper continues for Nursing and Medicine only. According to an OET customer-care email of November 2026, it stays available in 16 countries. This page lists those countries by region and the paper venues OET’s own finder shows in each one.
A listed venue is not a promise of a date or a seat, and OET’s data does not show whether an older paper venue continues in 2027. Confirm and book through the official finder. Last verified: 27 November 2026.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 27 Nov 2026

At a glance
OET on Paper from January 2027
OET announcement of 16 November 2026 and OET’s venue finder.
01 Who Nursing and Medicine only.
02 Where 16 countries, according to OET customer care. Never guaranteed.
03 First dates 22, 23, 29 and 30 January 2027.
The rule from January 2027
OET published the change on 16 November 2026 ( oet.com ).
OET on Paper
From January 2027 it continues for Nursing and Medicine only.
Bookings for 2027 paper tests are open for those two professions, according to the oet.com homepage on 27 November 2026.
OET on Computer
It remains available for all 12 healthcare professions at approved test venues, subject to availability.
The test content, length and marking are the same in both modes.
The 16 countries, by region
OET’s announcement does not name any country, and no page on oet.com lists them. The list below comes from an email from OET’s customer care team (Cambridge Boxhill Language Assessment) in November 2026: from 2027, OET on Paper is available for Nursing and Medicine candidates in these 16 countries only.
Region Countries where OET on Paper continues from January 2027
Middle East and Africa Egypt , Saudi Arabia , United Arab Emirates , Turkey , Ghana , Kenya
Europe United Kingdom , Ireland
Asia India , Pakistan , Nepal , Sri Lanka , Philippines
Oceania and North America Australia , New Zealand , Canada
The list limits paper, not computer
OET on Computer stays available for all 12 professions at approved venues, including in countries that are not on this list. See the full test-centre directory .
Being on the list guarantees nothing
Paper still depends on approved venues, dates and seats in each country. If OET publishes the list on oet.com, or changes it, the official page is the one to follow.
Paper venues in each of the 16 countries
These are the paper venue records in OET’s finder for each country, with a flag on the records OET added for January 2027.

Venues as listed in the OET venue finder on 27 November 2026, with names and addresses as OET keys them. For computer venues in these and other countries, see the OET test-centre directory .
How to read the January 2027 flag
OET’s finder holds two kinds of paper record. They do not mean the same thing.
Flagged: added for 2027
33 paper records carry the title &ldquo;Online Speaking test at venue&rdquo; and a note about January 2027. They are the newest paper records in OET’s data and they match the announcement that Speaking may run over a live video connection at the venue. We read them as the venues set up for the 2027 paper test. That is our reading of the titles and the note, not a statement by OET.
Not flagged: older paper listings
The other paper records are older listings. OET’s data has no end date and no status for them, so it does not show whether each one continues after December 2026. Never assume that a centre which ran paper tests in 2026 will run them in 2027.
Turkey and Sri Lanka
The flagged records appear in 14 of the 16 countries. Turkey and Sri Lanka each have one older paper record and no flagged record yet. Both are on the customer-care list, so check the finder for a 2027 paper date before you plan on paper there.
What to do with a flag
Treat it as a strong hint, not as availability. Search your city in the official finder and check that it offers a bookable paper date for your profession.
2026 and 2027, side by side
Paper tests booked for 2026 go ahead as booked. The change applies to tests from January 2027.

If your profession is not Nursing or Medicine
Your format is the computer test
Pharmacists, physiotherapists, dentists, radiographers, vets and the other professions take OET on Computer at an approved venue from January 2027, wherever they are. Find computer venues by country and city in the OET test-centre directory .
Switch your preparation now
Type every practice letter, read on screen and practise Listening with headphones. See computer vs paper: how to prepare and the computer-based practice .
OET@Home is a separate question Whether you can book OET@Home, and whether your regulator accepts it, are two different rules. Neither follows from the paper change. Read the OET@Home guide before you count on it.
Speaking and Listening on paper from 2027
What OET’s announcement says about test day.
Speaking
Paper candidates still attend an approved venue for the Speaking sub-test. Depending on the venue, you meet the interlocutor in person or over a live video connection.
Listening
At venues where Speaking runs over video, candidates are given headphones for both Speaking and Listening. The Listening audio plays through the headphones, with timing information shown on screen.
Booking, ID and fee Paper tests are booked through your myOET account, bring the same original ID you booked with, and OET’s fee is AU$587. The steps and the ID rule are in the test-centre directory . Nurses and doctors can prepare with the OET course for nurses or the OET course for doctors .

Frequently asked questions
Which countries have OET paper test centres in 2027?
According to an OET customer-care email from November 2026, OET on Paper continues from January 2027 in 16 countries: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, Ghana, Kenya, the United Kingdom, Ireland, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, Australia, New Zealand and Canada. The list is not published on oet.com.
Who can take OET on Paper from January 2027?
Nursing and Medicine candidates only. OET announced this on 16 November 2026. The other ten professions take OET on Computer at an approved venue.
Will my 2026 paper test centre still run paper tests in 2027?
Do not assume so. OET's venue data does not show whether an older paper listing continues in 2027. Search the official finder for your city and check that a 2027 paper date is offered before you plan around it.
What does the January 2027 flag on a venue mean?
It marks a paper venue record that OET added with the title Online Speaking test at venue and a note about January 2027. We read these as venues set up for the 2027 paper test with Speaking by video at the venue. That is our reading of OET's data, not a statement by OET.
What are the OET paper test dates in January 2027?
OET has published 23 and 30 January 2027 in its Global table and 22, 23, 29 and 30 January 2027 in its Americas table, for Nursing and Medicine. Bookings close 24 days before the test date, subject to change.
Is Speaking by video at a paper venue the same as OET@Home?
No. You still attend an approved venue for every sub-test. At some venues the Speaking interlocutor joins over a live video connection. OET@Home is a different test mode, taken on your own computer.
Is a paper seat guaranteed in the 16 countries?
No. Paper availability depends on approved venues and dates in each country, and seats can fill. Confirm in the official finder before you plan around a paper date.

## OET Clubbing Rules 2027: Combining Two Sittings | Dr Hesham

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-clubbing-rules.html

Which regulators let you combine two OET sittings in 2027: NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC, CORU and New Zealand rules, floors, time windows and single sub-test retakes.

Pathway Guides
OET clubbing rules 2027: who lets you combine two sittings
Clubbing means using the results of two OET sittings together to meet one score requirement. OET does not decide whether you can do it: your regulator does. Some regulators publish clear two-sitting rules, many accept one sitting only, and the conditions are different almost everywhere.
This guide sets out, regulator by regulator, what each one's own website says about combining sittings: the scores, the floor in every sitting, the time window and the rule on single sub-test retakes. Where a regulator's page is silent, we say "not confirmed" instead of guessing.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 27 Nov 2026
Also in Arabic: اقرأ هذا الدليل بالعربية
Last verified: 27 November 2026, against each regulator's own page. Rules change without notice, so open the source link before you book.
See the rules table Check your scores
At a glance
Three kinds of rule
What the regulators' own pages said on 27 November 2026.
01 Two sittings allowed NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC, CORU and five New Zealand regulators, each with its own conditions.
02 One sitting only GMC, GPhC, ECFMG, Medical Council of Ireland, NMBI, PSI and others.
03 One-element retake HCPC only, within six months of the original test.
The short answer
Whether you can combine two OET sittings depends only on the organisation that will read your results. Here is the position in one glance.
Publish a two-sitting rule
UK: NMC (nurses, midwives, nursing associates).
Australia: Ahpra and the National Boards; ANMAC (nursing skills assessment).
Ireland: CORU (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, optometry, podiatry, radiography, speech and language therapy).
New Zealand: Medical Council, Nursing Council, Pharmacy Council, Physiotherapy Board, Occupational Therapy Board.
Canada: the nursing regulator in Manitoba (CRNM) refers to two sittings, but its OET scores are not confirmed.
Require one sitting
UK: GMC (doctors), GPhC (pharmacists).
USA: ECFMG (doctors).
Ireland: Medical Council, NMBI (nurses and midwives), PSI (pharmacists).
New Zealand: Dental Council, Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Board, Veterinary Council.
Canada: CPSBC (doctors, British Columbia), CNO (nurses, Ontario), the NAPRA model policy for pharmacists.
Singapore: the medical, pharmacy, dental and allied health councils.
Something else, or silent
HCPC (UK): accepts a retake of one element within six months. Combining two full sittings is not stated.
Not confirmed: the Australian Department of Home Affairs (visas), TruMerit (US nurses), NABP (US pharmacists) and several smaller boards say nothing about combining OET sittings.
Before you rely on any of this A regulator can change its English language rule at any time. Treat this page as a map, then read the regulator's own page (linked in every section below) on the day you book and again on the day you apply.
What clubbing means, and where OET stands
"Clubbing" is the word candidates use, and OET uses it too. In its Test Regulations , OET says that some recognising organisations accept clubbing of scores from tests taken on different dates, and tells candidates to check with their recognising organisation whether results must come from one sitting.
What OET itself says
The decision belongs to the regulator, not to OET.
Your first attempt must include all four sub-tests (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking). Without that you do not receive results.
Each sitting produces a Statement of Results with a score from 0 to 500 for each sub-test.
You share results with an organisation through your online OET account.
How long a result stays valid is decided by the organisation that recognises it, not by OET.
What OET does not say
One combined certificate: not confirmed. Neither the Test Regulations nor OET's results page says that OET merges two sittings into one document.
Our reading, which is an inference and not an OET statement: each sitting keeps its own Statement of Results, you share each one, and the regulator does the combining.
We found no OET help article that explains clubbing step by step. Ask your regulator how it wants to receive two sittings.
Grades and scores The NMC prints the bands like this: grade B is 350 to 440, grade C+ is 300 to 340 and grade C is 250 to 290. Some regulators write letters, some write numbers, and a few now use numbers that sit inside a band, such as 360 or 320.
OET clubbing rules by regulator
The table lists each regulator we read, whether it accepts two sittings, how many, the window between them, the minimum in every sitting and whether a single sub-test retake counts. "Not confirmed" means the regulator's own page does not state the point or could not be read.

Regulator data last checked: 27 November 2026. Each row links to the regulator's own page.
The regulators that allow combining, one by one
Scores are written in the order Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking unless a line says otherwise.
NMC (UK): nurses, midwives, nursing associates
Target: grade B (350 or above) in Listening, Reading and Speaking, and grade C+ (300 or above) in Writing. Across two sittings you need B in each of those three at least once, and one Writing score of at least C+.
Floor in every sitting: at least C+ (300) in Listening, Reading and Speaking, and at least C (250) in Writing.
Sittings and window: two sittings, taken within 12 months of each other.
All four sub-tests each time: yes. You cannot take or retake a single domain.
Formats: paper, computer and OET@Home, and OET@Home can be combined with a paper or computer sitting. OET Nursing only. OET cannot be combined with IELTS.
Validity clock: scores are valid for two years, and both sittings must fall within the two years before the NMC assesses your complete application.
Source: NMC, accepted English language tests: OET (last updated 8 March 2024).
Ahpra and the National Boards (Australia)
Target, tests taken on or after 23 April 2026: Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350, Speaking 360.
Floor in every sitting, same tests: Listening 320, Reading 340, Writing 350, Speaking 350.
Tests taken on or before 22 April 2026: B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing, with no component below C+ in either sitting. Which table applies depends on the date of the test, not the date you apply.
Sittings and window: one sitting, or a maximum of two within a 12-month period.
All four sub-tests each time: yes. Ahpra accepts a one-skill retake for IELTS only, not for OET.
Formats: paper, or computer at a test centre. OET@Home is not accepted. Results from different test providers cannot be combined.
Validity clock: two years before the date you lodge your application. With two sittings, the two years run from the earlier one.
Professions: the same scores for every National Board except the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Practice Board.
Source: Ahpra, accepted English language tests (page reviewed 23 April 2026).
ANMAC (Australia): nursing and midwifery skills assessment
Target: B in Listening, Reading and Speaking and C+ in Writing. The page still prints letter grades.
Floor in every sitting: no component below C+.
Sittings and window: one sitting, or a maximum of two in a 12-month period.
All four sub-tests each time: yes.
Formats: paper or computer tests taken in an authorised testing centre, from the same test provider.
Validity clock: results must be less than two years old.
Not confirmed: whether ANMAC now applies Ahpra's numbers of 23 April 2026. Its page has not published numeric equivalents and announces coming changes, so re-read it before you apply.
Source: ANMAC, full skills assessment (no page date).
CORU (Ireland): seven health and social care professions
Target: B (350) in three components and C+ (300) in one for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, optometry and podiatry. Radiography needs B (350) in all four. Speech and language therapy needs B at 400 in three components and B at 350 in one.
Floor in every sitting: no OET sub-test below C+. The page adds that the overall minimum score must be met on both sittings. Ask CORU how it applies that sentence to your scores.
Sittings and window: a maximum of two sittings. The repeat must be with the same test provider and within six months of the first test.
All four sub-tests each time: yes. CORU does not accept individual OET sub-tests.
Formats: the page's sentence on at-home tests is ambiguous, so OET@Home is not confirmed.
Validity clock: certificates dated within two years of the date you submit your application.
Source: CORU, language requirements (no page date).
Medical Council of New Zealand: doctors
Target: Speaking 350, Listening 350, Reading 350, Writing 300, in the OET Medicine test.
Floor in every sitting: no component below 300.
Sittings and window: one sitting, or a maximum of two in a 12-month period.
All four sub-tests each time: yes.
Formats: the policy does not mention OET@Home or the computer test: not confirmed.
Validity clock: within two years of your application for registration, or of your NZREX Clinical date.
Source: MCNZ, policy on English language requirements (September 2026).
Nursing Council of New Zealand: nurses
Target: 350 in Reading, Listening and Speaking and 300 in Writing.
Floor in every sitting: none is printed.
Sittings and window: the scores can be achieved over more than one sitting. All required scores must be met within 12 months of the first sitting, and all sittings must be completed within three years of starting your application.
Formats: an OET test centre, on paper or on computer. OET@Home is not accepted. OET and IELTS results cannot be mixed.
Source: Nursing Council, English language competence policy guidance (19 August 2022).
Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand
Target: B in each of the four components, in OET Occupational Therapy.
Sittings and window: you may combine (club) more than one attempt, but the standard must be reached within 12 months of sitting the first test.
Floor in every sitting: none is printed.
Validity clock: results no older than 24 months when submitted. OET@Home: not confirmed.
Source: OTBNZ, English language policy for registration (policy 704, version 2.0).
New Zealand: Pharmacy Council and Physiotherapy Board
Pharmacy Council: A or B in each of the four bands within two years of the application. If you do not reach every score at one sitting, results from earlier OET tests within a two-year period are accepted. The page prints no floor and no number of sittings. Source .
Physiotherapy Board: 350 in Reading, Listening and Speaking and 300 in Writing, from results less than two years old. OET scores may be obtained across two sittings in six months. Source (help portal, updated 5 June 2025).
Not confirmed for the Physiotherapy Board: the detail that all four areas must be sat both times with nothing below 300. We could read it only in a search extract, because the Board's own page blocked us. The help portal also says the Board does not accept composite results from multiple examinations, so ask the Board to confirm before you plan on two sittings.
Canada: one reference to two sittings The College of Registered Nurses of Manitoba's accepted measures document (effective 26 March 2025) asks for a language test within the past two years and mentions achieving the minimum scores across two sittings of the same test. The document does not print the test list or the OET scores, so both are not confirmed. The other Canadian regulators whose sitting rule we could read ask for one sitting.
Two worked examples
These candidates are invented to illustrate the rules. They are not real students and the scores are not real results.
Illustration 1: a nurse who qualifies under the NMC rules
Mariam sits OET Nursing twice, six months apart, with all four sub-tests each time.
Sitting Listening Reading Writing Speaking
First 360 330 310 350
Second 340 350 290 360
Neither sitting passes alone: Reading is 330 in the first, and Listening is 340 in the second.
Floors: Listening, Reading and Speaking are 300 or above in both sittings, and Writing is 250 or above in both (310 and 290).
Targets: Listening 360 (first), Reading 350 (second), Speaking 350 (first) and Writing 310 (first).
Window: six months apart, inside the 12 months.
Result: the two sittings meet the NMC's published combining rule, as long as both still fall within the two years before the NMC assesses her complete application.
Illustration 2: a physiotherapist who misses the Ahpra floor
Omar sits OET Physiotherapy twice at a test centre, four months apart, both after 23 April 2026.
Sitting Listening Reading Writing Speaking
First 360 370 340 360
Second 350 360 360 350
Between the two sittings he has reached every target once: Listening 360, Reading 370, Writing 360 and Speaking 360.
But the floor for Writing in every sitting is 350, and his first sitting has Writing 340.
Result: Ahpra's published rule does not let him combine these two sittings. The second sitting does not pass alone either, because Speaking is 350 and the minimum is 360.
What is left: his second sitting meets every floor (350, 360, 360, 350 against 320, 340, 350, 350). A third sitting within 12 months of it, with all four sub-tests, every floor met and Speaking at 360 or above, could be combined with it.
The lesson: under the table for tests from 23 April 2026, the Writing floor equals the Writing minimum. You need 350 in Writing in both sittings.
We checked both illustrations against the NMC and Ahpra pages linked above. They show how the published rules work. They are not a ruling on any real application: only the regulator decides.
Single sub-test retakes are not the same as clubbing
Clubbing combines two full sittings. A single sub-test retake means sitting only one part again, for example Writing alone. OET offers it. Most regulators do not accept it.
What OET offers
After a first test with all four sub-tests, OET's Test Regulations allow a candidate to book fewer than four on a later attempt, subject to the recognising organisation's requirements.
In a news post of 29 October 2026 , OET confirmed the option to retake an individual sub-test and told nurses to check whether their credentialling organisation and state board accept it.
From January 2027, OET on Paper continues for Nursing and Medicine only . Any retake option that depends on the paper test is therefore open only to those two professions. Everyone else books on computer.
What regulators accept
HCPC (UK): the only regulator we found that says it accepts an OET retake of one element. The retake must be completed within six months of the original test date. Source (page updated 5 November 2026).
Not accepted: the NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC, the Medical Council of New Zealand and CORU all require the four sub-tests in every sitting. The PSI in Ireland and the Dental Council of New Zealand say they do not accept one-skill retakes.
Not confirmed: TruMerit and the US state boards of nursing. TruMerit's pages are silent, and we did not research the state boards one by one.
HCPC scores, for reference The HCPC lists OET for podiatry, dietetics, occupational therapy, physiotherapy and radiography at a total of 1400 with no element below 300, and for speech and language therapy at a total of 1800 with no element below 400. It names the computer and paper tests. OET@Home and the combining of two full sittings are not stated on its page: not confirmed.
Regulators that require one sitting
For these bodies every required score must come from the same test. A strong result in an earlier sitting does not carry over.
Regulator Who What its page says Source

Common mistakes
Mistakes about the rule
Assuming every regulator clubs. The GMC, GPhC, ECFMG and many others do not.
Carrying one regulator's floor to another. The NMC's floors are C+, C+, C in Writing and C+. Ahpra's are 320, 340, 350 and 350. ANMAC's is nothing below C+.
Reading the target and forgetting the floor. One weak sub-test in the first sitting can make that sitting unusable.
Mixing OET with IELTS. The regulators that club want both results from the same test.
Mistakes about timing and format
Missing the window. 12 months for the NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC and the Medical Council of New Zealand. Six months for CORU and the Physiotherapy Board of New Zealand.
Forgetting the validity clock. For Ahpra the two years run from the earlier sitting, so a slow second sitting shortens the time you have to apply.
Booking one sub-test only. A single sub-test retake does not count for the NMC or Ahpra.
Using OET@Home where it is refused. The NMC accepts it. Ahpra, ANMAC and the Nursing Council of New Zealand do not.
Meeting registration but missing the visa. The Australian Department of Home Affairs asks for Writing 380 for Proficient English, while Ahpra registration asks for Writing 350.
What is not confirmed
We could not confirm these points from the organisations' own pages on 27 November 2026. Do not plan around them until the organisation tells you in writing.
OET and the UK
Whether OET issues a single combined certificate for two sittings.
HCPC: combining two full sittings, and OET@Home.
GDC: its guidance names only IELTS and does not mention OET at all.
Australia, USA and elsewhere
Department of Home Affairs (Australian visas): combining OET sittings. Its pages name retake schemes for other tests only.
ANMAC: numeric scores and whether the 23 April 2026 Ahpra figures apply.
TruMerit and US state boards of nursing: combining and single sub-test retakes.
NABP (US pharmacists): OET is accepted for tests taken on or after 11 January 2027, but the minimum scores, sitting rules and validity had not been published when we checked.
PSI super-scoring, the Dental Council of Ireland, the Veterinary Council of Ireland, and in New Zealand the radiography, dietetics and podiatry boards: no combining rule for OET could be read.
Gulf regulators: we found no published OET requirement on their websites, so there is no clubbing rule to report.
How to plan a second sitting
If your first result was close, a second sitting can finish the job, but only when it is planned around your regulator's rule.
Five steps
1. Name your regulator. Find it in the recognition matrix by profession and country and read its current scores in OET score requirements .
2. Test your first sitting against the floor. If one sub-test is under the floor, that sitting cannot be combined. Put your numbers into the OET score calculator .
3. Count the window and the validity clock. Choose a date from OET test dates and fees that sits inside both.
4. Choose a format your regulator accepts. Read the OET@Home guide before booking a home test, and remember that paper is for Nursing and Medicine only from January 2027.
5. Book all four sub-tests unless your regulator says in writing that it accepts a single sub-test retake.
Prepare the sub-test that held you back
A second sitting only helps if the weak score moves. Our guide to retaking OET after a near miss shows how to read your Statement of Results and build a short plan.

Frequently asked questions
What is OET clubbing?
Clubbing means using the results of two OET sittings together to meet a regulator's score requirement. OET does not decide whether it is allowed: each regulator sets its own rule, and many accept one sitting only.
Which regulators allow OET clubbing?
On the pages we read on 27 November 2026, the NMC, Ahpra and ANMAC publish two-sitting rules. So do CORU in Ireland and, in New Zealand, the Medical Council, the Nursing Council, the Pharmacy Council, the Physiotherapy Board and the Occupational Therapy Board. Each one sets different conditions.
Can I combine two OET results for the GMC?
No. The GMC asks for at least grade B in each of the four areas in the same test, from your most recent sitting.
How far apart can the two sittings be?
It depends on the regulator. The NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC and the Medical Council of New Zealand use a 12-month window. CORU and the Physiotherapy Board of New Zealand use six months.
Can I retake only one OET sub-test?
OET lets you book fewer than four sub-tests after a first full test, but most regulators do not accept the result. The NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC, the Medical Council of New Zealand and CORU want all four sub-tests in every sitting. The HCPC is the only regulator we found that accepts a retake of one element, within six months of the original test.
Does OET issue one certificate for two sittings?
This is not confirmed. OET's published pages do not say that it merges two sittings into one Statement of Results. Our reading is that each sitting keeps its own Statement of Results and the regulator does the combining. Confirm this with your regulator.
Can I combine an OET sitting with an IELTS sitting?
We found no regulator that allows it. The NMC, Ahpra, ANMAC, CORU and the Nursing Council of New Zealand all say both results must come from the same test.
Does OET@Home count in a combined result?
For the NMC, yes: it accepts OET@Home and lets you combine it with a paper or computer sitting. Ahpra, ANMAC and the Nursing Council of New Zealand do not accept OET@Home at all.

## Who Accepts OET? 12 Professions by Country (2027)

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/oet-recognition-by-country.html

Which regulators accept OET for each of the 12 professions in the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, the USA, Canada, Singapore and the Gulf, with sources.

Pathway Guides
Who accepts OET? The 12 professions by country and regulator
OET is not accepted "by a country". It is accepted, or not, by one regulator for one profession. A nurse and a dentist heading to the same country can get opposite answers.
This page takes each of the 12 OET professions and shows, destination by destination, which regulator names OET, at what scores, and where the regulator's own website does not say. Where we could not confirm a point, the page says "not confirmed". It never leaves a blank for you to fill with hope.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 27 Nov 2026
Last verified: 27 November 2026, against each regulator's own page. Recognition and scores change without notice, so open the source link before you book.
Find your profession Score requirements
At a glance
How recognition works
Three things to hold on to while you read the matrix.
01 Regulator, not country Each regulator decides for its own profession.
02 Not listed is not accepted A profession the regulator does not name is "not confirmed".
03 Visa is a separate test Immigration scores differ from registration scores.
OET has 12 profession versions
OET is an English test for healthcare professionals, and you sit it in the version for your own profession. The 12 versions are:
The 12 OET professions
Medicine Nursing Pharmacy Dentistry
Dietetics Occupational Therapy Optometry Physiotherapy
Podiatry Radiography Speech Pathology Veterinary Science
Recognition is decided regulator by regulator
A test version existing for your profession does not mean your regulator accepts it. The General Dental Council in the UK, for example, names only IELTS in its guidance, although OET Dentistry exists. In Canada, the pharmacy policy names OET while the physiotherapy and occupational therapy bodies do not list it.
"Not confirmed" is an answer, not a gap
OET's own website says its results are accepted worldwide and points to an organisation finder. That is OET's list. We rely on what each regulator publishes itself. When a regulator's page does not name OET for your profession, or we could not read the page, the status here is "not confirmed", never "accepted".
How to read the statuses
Every row in the matrix carries one status. They mean different things, and we keep them apart.
Status What it means What to do
Accepted The regulator's own page names OET for this profession and prints the scores. Read the scores, the validity period and the sitting rule on the source page, then book.
Conditional OET is named, but with a condition that changes the answer for some candidates: a start date, scores not yet published, or a limit on the test format. Read the condition first. Do not book until you know you meet it.
Not accepted The regulator says it accepts only other tests, or says it does not accept OET. Take one of the tests the regulator names.
Not listed The regulator publishes its list of English tests and OET is not on it. Treat it as not accepted unless the regulator tells you otherwise in writing.
Not confirmed We could not read the regulator's page, the page is silent, or the only evidence is second-hand. Ask the regulator in writing before paying for any test.
The matrix: 12 professions by destination and regulator
For each profession the matrix lists every destination and regulator we read, with its status, its minimum scores and a link to the regulator's own page. Scores are the regulator's figures on the date shown. A profession with no entry for a destination was not found on that regulator's pages and is "not confirmed".

Regulator data last checked: 27 November 2026. Every row links to its source.
Destination by destination
A short reading of each destination, with the guide that covers the full route. The matrix above has the scores.
United Kingdom
The GMC (doctors), the NMC (nurses, midwives and nursing associates) and the GPhC (pharmacists) each name OET. The HCPC lists OET scores for six professions: podiatry, dietetics, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, physiotherapy and radiography. The General Dental Council's guidance names only IELTS and does not mention OET, so dentistry is not confirmed. Optometry and veterinary science in the UK are not confirmed.
UK pathway guide
Ireland
Ireland has the widest published coverage we found. NMBI (nurses and midwives), the Medical Council, the PSI (pharmacists) and the Dental Council each name OET, and CORU names it for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, optometry, podiatry, radiography and speech and language therapy. For veterinary science, we could not read the Veterinary Council of Ireland's page: not confirmed.
Ireland pathway guide
Australia
Ahpra says all National Boards, except the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Practice Board, accept the same tests at the same scores. For tests taken on or after 23 April 2026 that is Listening 350, Reading 360, Writing 350 and Speaking 360, and OET@Home is not accepted. A profession without its own OET version can use the OET test of another registered profession. ANMAC names OET for the nursing and midwifery skills assessment. If your profession is not registered through a National Board, OET recognition is not confirmed here.
Australia pathway guide
New Zealand
Eleven of the 12 professions have a board that names OET: medicine, nursing, pharmacy, physiotherapy, dentistry, occupational therapy, radiography, dietetics, podiatry, optometry and veterinary science. Scores and sitting rules differ from board to board, and several boards say nothing about OET@Home. For speech pathology we read no primary source: not confirmed.
New Zealand pathway guide
United States
ECFMG accepts OET Medicine for its 2027 Pathways. TruMerit, formerly CGFNS, lists OET for nurses in its Certification Program and does not accept at-home tests. NABP will accept OET Pharmacy for FPGEC certification for tests taken on or after 11 January 2027, but had not published the minimum scores when we checked: see OET for pharmacists in the USA . State boards of nursing and the other nine professions are not confirmed.
USA pathway guide
Canada
There is no national licence, so the answer changes by province. The medical colleges of British Columbia and Alberta name OET Medicine. The nursing regulators of Ontario and British Columbia name OET, while Alberta's (CRNA) lists only CELBAN and IELTS Academic. The NAPRA model policy and the Ontario College of Pharmacists name OET for pharmacists. The bodies we read for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, dentistry in Ontario and veterinary medicine do not list OET. Other provinces and professions are not confirmed.
Canada pathway guide
Singapore
The Singapore Medical Council, Pharmacy Council and Dental Council name OET, and the Allied Health Professions Council names it for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language therapy and radiography. All ask for the scores in a single sitting. The Singapore Nursing Board's page for foreign-trained nurses lists no English test at all, so OET for nurses is not confirmed. Dietetics, podiatry, optometry and veterinary science are not confirmed.
Singapore pathway guide
The Gulf
We found no published OET requirement on the Gulf regulators' websites as of 27 November 2026. That covers the DHA, DOH and MOHAP in the United Arab Emirates, the SCFHS in Saudi Arabia, the DHP in Qatar, the OMSB and Ministry of Health in Oman, the Ministry of Health in Kuwait and the NHRA in Bahrain. Licensing runs through each regulator's own exam and credential verification. This is not the same as "OET is not accepted": confirm with the regulator or your employer.
Gulf pathway guide
Preparing from the region Many candidates prepare in Egypt or the Gulf for registration elsewhere. Our country pages cover test venues and preparation locally: Egypt , Saudi Arabia , the UAE , Qatar , Kuwait and Oman .
Immigration is separate from registration
A visa office and a health regulator are two different readers of your result. Meeting one does not meet the other.
Australia: Department of Home Affairs
Accepts OET for visa purposes at its own scores.
Tests on or after 7 August 2025: Competent English is Listening 290, Reading 310, Writing 290, Speaking 330. Proficient English is 350, 360, 380 and 360.
Results from within the three years before the visa application, depending on the visa subclass.
OET@Home is not accepted.
Proficient English needs Writing 380, while Ahpra registration needs Writing 350.
Source: Home Affairs .
Immigration New Zealand
Lists OET for skilled residence visas.
Principal applicants need grade C+ or higher in all four skills.
The test must be sat in person at a test centre, and the result must be no more than two years old.
C+ is lower than the New Zealand health regulators' requirements, so a visa-level score does not satisfy registration.
Other visa categories: not confirmed.
Source: Immigration New Zealand .
Canada: IRCC
IRCC does not list OET as an approved language test for Express Entry.
The approved English tests on its page are CELPIP, IELTS and PTE Core.
If you need both immigration and registration, you may need two different tests.
Other IRCC programmes: not confirmed.
Source: IRCC (page dated 16 October 2026).
What to do when your profession or regulator is "not confirmed"
"Not confirmed" does not mean no. It means nobody should spend your test fee on an assumption.
Ask the regulator four questions, in writing
Do you accept OET for my profession, and which OET profession version?
What is the minimum score in each sub-test, and how old can the result be?
Must all scores come from one sitting, or can two be combined?
Do you accept OET@Home, or only a test taken at a test centre?
While you wait for the answer
Do not rely on a forum post, an agent or another preparation site. Keep the regulator's written reply.
Check whether your employer or visa route asks for a different test from the regulator.
If the regulator names another test only, prepare for that test. Your clinical English practice still counts.
Keep preparing: free practice and the free placement test cost you nothing while you wait.
Next steps once your regulator is confirmed
Check the rules that sit beside the score
OET score requirements : the score each regulator asks for.

OET@Home : who can book it, and which regulators accept it.

Frequently asked questions
Which countries accept OET?
No country accepts OET as a whole. Each health regulator decides for its own profession. On the pages we read on 27 November 2026, regulators in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Canada and Singapore name OET for at least one profession.
Is OET accepted for all 12 professions?
No. OET has 12 profession versions, but a regulator may name only some of them. A profession that a regulator does not list is not confirmed, and you should ask the regulator before booking.
Is OET accepted in Canada?
Partly. Some provincial regulators for medicine, nursing and pharmacy name OET. The national bodies we read for physiotherapy, occupational therapy and veterinary medicine do not list it, and IRCC does not list OET for Express Entry.
Do Gulf regulators require OET?
We found no published OET requirement on the Gulf regulators' websites as of 27 November 2026. Licensing there runs through each regulator's own exam and credential verification. Confirm with the regulator or your employer.
Can I use OET for a visa?
Sometimes. The Australian Department of Home Affairs and Immigration New Zealand accept OET at their own scores, which differ from the registration scores. IRCC does not list OET for Express Entry to Canada.
Does the General Dental Council accept OET?
Not confirmed. The GDC's guidance names only IELTS and does not mention OET. It says it will consider other credible evidence, which is not a promise. Ask the GDC before you book.
Is OET accepted for nurses in the USA?
TruMerit, formerly CGFNS, lists OET for its Certification Program at Listening 320, Reading 340, Writing 350 and Speaking 360, and does not accept at-home tests. State boards of nursing set their own rules, which we have not confirmed.

## Ireland Pathway Guide 2027: NMBI, Medical Council, CORU

URL: https://oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/ireland-pathway-guide.html

Ireland pathway guide for OET candidates: NMBI, Medical Council, PSI, CORU and Dental Council scores, sittings, validity and OET@Home rules, with sources.

Ireland Pathway Guide - Edition 2027
Ireland Pathway Guide 2027 for OET Candidates
Ireland has no single health regulator. Each profession has its own body, its own OET score line and its own rule on sittings and OET@Home. This guide sets them side by side for all 12 OET professions, with the official page for each rule.
By Dr Ahmed Hesham , medical doctor and founder of OET with Dr Hesham · Published 27 Nov 2026

Ireland overview
Choose your regulator first, then your test
In Ireland the regulator depends on your profession: NMBI for nurses and midwives, the Medical Council for doctors, PSI for pharmacists, CORU for seven of the allied health professions that OET covers, the Dental Council for dentists and the Veterinary Council of Ireland for vets. OET is accepted by the first five, each with a different score line. Confirm the accepted test, the score and the format on your regulator's page before you pay for any test.
Important: This guide is educational orientation only. It is not legal, immigration or regulator advice, and regulators can change their rules without notice. We are an independent OET coaching service. We are not affiliated with OET, with any regulator or with any test centre, and test centres are not our locations.
Profession Regulator Is OET accepted? Minimum OET score Sittings OET@Home
Nursing and midwifery NMBI Accepted (OET Nursing) Grade B in three components and C+ in one One result only, no combined results Not accepted
Medicine Medical Council Accepted (OET Medicine) Grade B in each module Single sitting Not accepted
Pharmacy PSI Accepted (OET Pharmacy) Listening 350, Reading 350, Speaking 350, Writing 300 All four at the same sitting, no one-skill retakes Not accepted (home-based tests)
Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, optometry CORU Accepted (your profession's OET) Grade B (350) in three components and C+ (300) in one Maximum two sittings, with conditions Not confirmed : ask CORU
